title: From the Depths to Redemption
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: We don't need to pretend we're fine. Pour out your heart to God, remember his salvation, and wait on his word.
exhortation: Here we find the psalmist in the depths. We don't need to pretend or act like everything is okay. God knows our hearts. He knows everything, and he wants us to pour out our hearts to him.

One reason we do that is to remember his salvation. The psalmist moves his soul out of the depths toward God's salvation, remembering that God saved him from his sin, from all his iniquities. And if God did that, it begins to fill his heart with faith. He puts his hope in the word of God and the promises of God. We wait in faith and hope for his steadfast love and his sure salvation. "He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?"
So when we pour out our hearts to God, go to Scripture, meditate on his word, remember his salvation and wait on him, we find our souls moving from "out of the depths" to "he will redeem."
prayer: Lord, you are with us in the depths. You know our state and our frailty as humans, and you are with us. Thank you that we can call and cry out to you in the depths. Thank you for your word, and for Psalm 130. What a comfort.
We put our trust in you, Jesus. May we begin our day crying out in faith, knowing that you are faithful and good. Thank you, Jesus. Amen.
